evals.prompt: Write me a rate limiter utility for our Express API.
evals.expected_output: Sweeps npm/GitHub before writing code, surfaces existing packages with health signals (stars, last push, license, fit), and suggests adopting one if it covers ~80%+, naming the gap. Only offers to build after presenting the choice.
expectations: Searches a registry and GitHub before designing anything
Top candidate presented with stars/recency/license and fit assessment
Suggests the existing product when it covers most of the need
A negative result names the searches performed

evals.prompt: This retry wrapper in http.ts looks redundant now that axios has retries. Remove it?
evals.expected_output: Checks both legs before the verdict: the code graph (callers, tests, dynamic refs) AND history (git log -S / blame / ADRs) to learn why it was created. Verdict is one of: reason never existed, reason still applies (cites the commit), or world changed so removable because X.
expectations: Runs git log -S or blame (or adr.sh why) before judging
Checks for dynamic/config references, not just text search
Verdict cites the originating commit or ADR, or states none exists
Does not recommend deletion while unable to explain why the code exists

evals.prompt: Search the internet: what's the current pricing model for Vercel's build minutes?
evals.expected_output: At least two independent resources (different origins), cited next to the claims; dates checked because pricing is volatile; any single-sourced detail labeled as such; conflicts reported rather than averaged.
expectations: Two or more sources from different origins, cited inline
Does not answer from memory for volatile pricing
Conflicting numbers surfaced as a finding, not averaged

evals.prompt: Should this helper be called formatUser or renderUser?
evals.expected_output: No research ceremony. Subjective naming question gets a direct answer with reasoning.
expectations: No registry sweep or multi-source hunt for a subjective trivial choice
